application_guidance.input_pattern: Convex expected-value minimization with exact Euclidean projection and a known full stochastic-subgradient second-moment bound.
read_original_when: Changing sampling dependence, oracle bias, norm, projection accuracy or output.
Using sliding averages, large deviations or mirror descent instead of this extracted result.
sensitive_conditions: Use the initial-point radius D_X, not an unexplained diameter convention.
Use the weighted average for general steps; constant steps produce the arithmetic average.
The selected guarantee concerns expectation and the averaged output.

complexity_scope.guarantee: For each admissible instance and each finite N; expectation over fresh oracle samples.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: All constants in the displayed bounds are explicit.
complexity_scope.oracle: Fresh iid sampling and unbiased stochastic subgradient with uniformly bounded full Euclidean second moment; exact Euclidean projection.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Feasible average of x_1,...,x_N; expectation of objective gap f(bar x_N)-f_*.
complexity_scope.regime: All N>=1 and finite positive M; specialized step additionally requires D_X>0 and the horizon/radius/moment information before sampling.
complexity_scope.resource: N sample draws, N stochastic-subgradient calls and N projections for the stated N-update recurrence; projection/estimator computation is separately charged. No wall-clock complexity is asserted.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Projected Euclidean SA recurrence with full-horizon stepsize-weighted average; the constant-step specialization is alg.P015.robust_sa, variant selected.

content.intended_use: An upper guarantee for a particular averaged-output Algorithm; no unrestricted Oracle Complexity lower claim.

map: Eq.(1.5) and (2.3) bound half the squared distance after projection by the preceding distance, the stochastic inner product and half gamma_t squared times the oracle norm squared.
Eq.(2.4) conditions on prior iid samples; Eq.(2.5) then gives Eq.(2.6). Convexity bounds expected objective gap by the expected subgradient inner product.
Eq.(2.14) sums the resulting inequalities; squared-distance terms telescope and the terminal nonnegative term is discarded.
Eq.(2.15) divides by the positive stepsize sum. Eq.(2.16) and convexity give the averaged-output bound; the initial distance satisfies a_1<=D_X^2/2, yielding Eq.(2.18a).
For constant gamma, Eq.(2.19) is (D_X^2+M^2 N gamma^2)/(2N gamma). Substitution of Eq.(2.20) gives Eq.(2.21).
proofs.omitted_details: This records the source's displayed argument, not a new local Theorem or independent reproof. No external cited result is needed beyond the projection/convexity facts displayed in the checked passages.
proofs.reading_coverage: Actually read the selected proof passages and visually checked their equations on derived original-page images for PDF pages 3,4,6,7. A1–A2 and model checked on pages 1–2.

assumptions: The sequence xi_1,xi_2,... is iid with the distribution of xi; x_t is a measurable function of xi_1,...,xi_{t-1}.
The stochastic oracle has well-defined g(x)=E[G(x,xi)] in the subdifferential of f at x for every x in X, so E[G(x_t,xi_t) given prior history]=g(x_t).
There is a finite positive M such that E||G(x,xi)||_2^2<=M^2 for every x in X.
Stepsizes are deterministic and strictly positive. Smoothness, strong convexity and an interior minimizer are not required.
statement.conclusion: bar x_N belongs to X and E[f(bar x_N)-f_*] <= (D_X^2+M^2 sum_{t=1}^N gamma_t^2)/(2 sum_{t=1}^N gamma_t). In particular, for D_X>0 and gamma_t=D_X/(M sqrt(N)) for t=1,...,N, E[f(bar x_N)-f_*] <= D_X M/sqrt(N).
statement.objects_and_definitions: Let n,d be positive integers, X a nonempty bounded closed convex subset of R^n, and xi a random vector supported on Xi subset R^d. Let f(x)=E[F(x,xi)] be finite, continuous and convex on X. Fix deterministic x_1 in X and write D_X=max_{x in X}||x-x_1||_2 and f_*=min_X f. For deterministic positive steps gamma_t, define x_{t+1}=Pi_X(x_t-gamma_t G(x_t,xi_t)), S_N=sum_{t=1}^N gamma_t and bar x_N=sum_{t=1}^N gamma_t x_t/S_N. Pi_X is exact Euclidean metric projection.
statement.parameter_domains: n,d,N are positive integers; 0<M<infinity; 0<=D_X<infinity; 0<gamma_t<infinity. The specialized step requires 0<D_X<infinity.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every instance satisfying these assumptions, every deterministic initial point and positive deterministic stepsize sequence, and every integer N>=1, the general bound holds with expectation over the iid samples. For the constant-step specialization choose N before sampling and assume D_X>0.
